title: More on the Classics Rule in this video: @Joe Weinberg   #broadway #t...
transcript: do you remember the offhand comment Neil Patrick Harris made in his Tony speech that got the Tony Awards to change their eligibility rules? if not, welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history it's important to know that in 2014 Neil Patrick Harris was quite the Tony darling but in his own unique way he had never been nominated before but he hosted the ceremony four times in five years and immediately afterward won a Tony for himself playing the title role in Hedwig and the Angry Inch during his speech he was saying thank you to the writers of Hedwig John Cameron Mitchell and Steven Trask and said this and it's a disappointment that you guys weren't able to be up for your categories given the circumstances so thank you for doing that the reason they weren't eligible is because like many Broadway productions in the 21st century Hedwig and the Angry Inch fell under the classics rule where it was deemed a revival even though it had never been on Broadway before pause for a second and say that the classics rule, in my opinion, is a good thing I think the rule itself could use some re-wording but the way it's been implemented I think has been very positive I sometimes joke that it's the “call a spade a spade” rule where like, did they revive it? then it's a revival why does it matter if it hasn't been on Broadway before? but going back to the point here the unfortunate side effect is that the writers of these shows were not able to compete in the best book, best score category etc. the revival Tony Awards went to the producers, not the writers or at least that was the case until Tony Darling Neil Patrick Harris decided to use his moment in the spotlight to call that out and only three days later they announced a rule change that is in effect to the this day *now* if a show falls under the classics rule where it's nominated in one of the revival categories despite having never been on Broadway before the writers of the show are included in the nomination the same way they do for the playwrights in the best play category so while John Cameron Mitchell and Stephen Trask unfortunately never got their chance to be nominated for Hedwig something like 16 very well deserving writers since then have been able to receive Tony Awards or Tony nominations because of this rule of course John Cameron Mitchell did end up getting some Tony recognition for Hedwig as a special Tony Award the very next year For reprising the role he originated as a replacement in this Broadway revival now admittedly, we don't know for a fact that Neil Patrick Harris's comment is what inspired the rule change it's speculation based on circumstantial evidence but you have to admit that the timing combined with Neil Patrick Harris's status as basically the face of the Tony Awards at the time feels a little too perfect
